# 100-the-phase-demonstrations — info

*Generated by `104` from the folds in `100-the-phase-demonstrations.lua`. Do not edit this page;
edit the program and run the sweep again.*

**An instrument** — phase 14. Not part of the machine, and it does not ship
to whoever builds one.

## What it is

One demonstration per phase. Each loads the whole blueprint set, picks out
that phase's files, and shows what the phase actually produced: its headline
numbers with live values, every constraint it asserts and whether it holds,
and what it left open.

For a general reader: this project's deliverable is a set of blueprints in
which no number is written twice, so a demonstration of it cannot be a
program doing something -- it is the design answering questions about itself.
Every figure printed below is resolved from the blueprints at the moment you
run it. Change a dimension and run it again and the numbers move.

## What it offers

Nothing. This file is run rather than loaded, so it publishes no names.

## How it works inside

Nothing outside this file can call these. They are listed so a reader
knows what is in it, not how — a companion page treats a function as a
box with a label on it.

| function | takes | what it is for |
|---|---|---|
| `bar` | `ch` | *(no description in the source)* |
| `fmt` | `L, name` | *(no description in the source)* |
| `show_phase` | `R, n` | *(no description in the source)* |
| `show_instruments` | `R` | Phase 14 has no design numbers of its own. |

## What it reads

`091`, `092`, `095`, `102`. Every instrument here reaches for its dependencies with `dofile`
against a hard-coded project root rather than with `require`, because
there is no package path to configure and a root that can be overridden
by an argument is this project's convention for anything runnable.

## Running it

It is a module. Something else loads it; there is nothing to run.

comment carrying its name, followed by prose, followed by the definition.
That was adopted so a long file collapses neatly in an editor. It is also,
by accident, a machine-readable statement of what a module offers, and it
is the only reason this page can exist — Lua itself says nothing about what
a file exports.*
